tb21_profile.skill: Provision an awkward statistical toolchain (RStan at a pinned version, needing a C++ compiler from R), then translate a stated hierarchical Bayesian model - binomial likelihood, Beta group priors, an improper (alpha+beta)^(-5/2) hyperprior - into correct Stan code and read posterior means back within tolerance.
tb21_profile.domain: R / Stan / rstan, Bayesian hierarchical modelling and MCMC; CRAN and system build dependencies.
tb21_profile.task_form: Configure-a-toolchain plus implement-from-spec, graded on numeric posterior means written to plain-text files.

verifier_notes: No grade looked wrong enough to re-read tests. Nothing in any pool actually authors a Stan file with an improper hyperprior, so the ranking splits the task: CalibForge covers the modelling and Stan-reading half, Terminal-Lego's R-package-build cluster covers the install half. No FREE candidate appears anywhere in per_source for this task except none at all - scientific-computing_20260503_030115_002 and data-science_20260617_051646_007 are both FREE and were deliberately dropped despite being on-topic hierarchical-Bayes tasks.
searches: tools.py search all "\b(Stan|rstan|cmdstan|pystan|PyMC|JAGS|brms|NUTS|Hamiltonian Monte Carlo|Metropolis[- ]Hastings|Gibbs sampl|MCMC)\b"
tools.py search all "(Beta\(alpha, ?beta\)|beta-binomial|Binomial\(n_i|hierarchical Bayesian|posterior mean|hyperprior|partial pooling)"

Validate a custom MCMC sampler against a closed-form solution; teaches checking that chains actually converged to the right posterior.
Beta-Binomial conjugate posterior mean and variance from prior plus counts; the analytic check a solver needs to sanity-test Stan output.
Metropolis-Hastings on count data with several parallel chains plus a KDE MAP estimate; multi-chain posterior summarisation.

Fit a Bayesian linear regression and report posterior summaries from a CSV; posterior estimation, simpler model.
Implement a random-walk Metropolis sampler in C for regression coefficients with a Gaussian likelihood; sampler mechanics from scratch.
Drive Rscript from a shell pipeline to compute a bootstrap CI and compare against a baseline; R invocation and numeric tolerance.
Bayesian A/B comparison of two campaigns from daily counts; binomial-style comparison, shallower than a hierarchical fit.

notes: No corpus contains a task that writes a Stan model, so the honest answer splits the TB2.1 task in two. CalibForge owns the Bayesian-modelling half and is far ahead: it has tasks that read a .stan file and must reproduce its priors and likelihood exactly, an R/TMB task whose shape (pinned CRAN install needing a C++ toolchain, model template, /app/analysis.R, single-number txt outputs) matches this task almost line for line, and several hierarchical-divergence repairs. Terminal-Lego-15k turned out unexpectedly useful - not through anything retrieval surfaced (its shortlist was generic sklearn/pandas filler) but through its cluster of 'R package fails to build because a system library is missing' tasks, which is the actual failure mode of installing RStan 2.32.7; that cluster is the only reason a Lego entry reaches final_top10. TMax contributes two genuine Beta-Binomial conjugate tasks, one of which uses the same successes/trials column shape. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has nothing Bayesian at all; its best offering is pinned-version environment provisioning and all of it is 'absent'. SWE-Smith is the weakest corpus here - no Bayesian or R content, so its bottom half is quota filler at overall 2. SWE-Rebench does better than expected via pymc, numpyro and a jax beta-binomial logpmf bug.
